correctness.rationale: With any rational origin on the genus-one curve, write G=C(F_q) and T=[H-3O] in Pic^0(F_q). A line through three distinct rational points has group sum T; pairs of distinct points admit a rational tangent line when 2a+b=T or a+2b=T. Four covering lines must partition the twelve points into four distinct collinear triples, so sum(G)=4T. In cyclic C_12, sum(G)=6, which is not in 4G; four lines are impossible. For C_2 x C_6, sum(G)=0 and 4T=0 exactly when T lies in 3G, equivalent to a rational flex. Six explicitly inspected finite line certificates cover G with four lines only in this latter case and with five otherwise; the geometric group-to-line argument lifts them to any characteristic. An independent hypergraph generator constructed all tangent/secant rational line-point subsets and independently optimized exact set cover by dynamic programming over 2^12 subsets: minimum counts for C12 T=0,1,2 were 5,5,5; for C2xC6 T=0,1,2 were 4,5,5. The two F11 examples were independently checked to have 12 points and the predicted 2-torsion counts.
